title: Allergic Reaction & Hives in Cabo: A Doctor 24/7
description: Hives or an allergic reaction on vacation in Cabo? Know when to call 911, what to do next and how to get a doctor to your hotel for $189 USD, tax included.
h1: Allergic reactions and hives on vacation in Cabo: what to do
image_alt: Doctor and pharmacy support for a traveler with an allergic reaction in Cabo San Lucas

intro: A new seafood dish, a different sunscreen, an insect you never saw: a vacation puts your body in contact with a lot of unfamiliar things in a short time. If your skin suddenly breaks out in itchy welts in Los Cabos, it helps to know what can wait a few hours and what cannot wait at all.

Call 911 right away if there is any trouble breathing, swelling of the tongue or throat, fainting or a reaction that is spreading fast. For milder symptoms, this guide covers common triggers, sensible first steps and how to get an English-speaking doctor to your hotel, villa or yacht.

p: Anaphylaxis is a severe, whole-body allergic reaction that can become life-threatening within minutes. It does not always start with a rash. Call 911 immediately if you or someone with you has any of these, especially after a food, sting or medication:
list: Difficulty breathing, wheezing, a tight chest or noisy breathing
Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, a hoarse voice or trouble swallowing
Feeling faint, confused or very weak, passing out, or a rapid, weak pulse
Hives or flushing together with vomiting, cramps or diarrhea that start suddenly
Pale, gray or bluish skin or lips
A sense that something is very wrong, particularly if you have had a severe reaction before
p_after: If the person has a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector, use it right away as their doctor instructed, then still call 911. Symptoms can return after they seem to improve, so emergency evaluation is needed. Have the person lie down, or sit up if breathing is hard, and do not let them stand or walk around.
An antihistamine is not a substitute for epinephrine or emergency care. Do not wait for a house call or a message reply in these situations.

sections.h2: What hives look and feel like
p: Hives (urticaria) are raised, itchy welts. They may be pink, red or close to your normal skin tone, and they can be as small as a pencil eraser or merge into large patches. A typical clue is that individual welts move around: one fades within hours while another appears somewhere else.

Hives on their own are often uncomfortable rather than dangerous, but they can be the first sign of a bigger reaction. Watch closely for any of the warning signs above, particularly in the first couple of hours after a likely trigger.

Not every itchy rash is hives. Heat rash, sunburn, sun-related rashes, contact reactions to plants or lotions, insect bites and skin infections can look similar at first and are managed differently. If your skin is mostly burned, blistered or painful after a beach day, read our guide to sunburn and sun poisoning in Cabo.

sections.h2: Common triggers on a Cabo vacation
p: Sometimes the cause is obvious, and often it is not. These are worth thinking through with a doctor:
list: Food and drinks. Shrimp and other shellfish, fish, nuts, peanuts and sesame can appear in ceviche, sauces, mole or cocktails.
Medications. Antibiotics, anti-inflammatory pain relievers and other new medicines or supplements are possible causes.
Stings and bites. Bees, wasps, ants and scorpions on land, or jellyfish in the water.
Skin products. A new sunscreen, after-sun gel, massage oil, fragrance, temporary tattoo or resort laundry detergent.
Physical triggers. Heat, sweating, sunlight, pressure from straps or even cool water can set off hives in some people.
Infections. A viral illness can cause hives without any true allergy.
p_after: A scorpion sting deserves prompt medical attention, and it is an emergency for young children, older adults or anyone with trouble breathing or swallowing, drooling, muscle twitching or unusual eye movements.

sections.h2: First steps for a mild reaction
p: If breathing is normal, there is no swelling of the mouth or throat and you feel otherwise well, these steps can help while you arrange advice:
list: Stop using or eating the suspected trigger.
Rinse off new lotions or sunscreen with cool water and mild soap.
Apply a cool compress, wear loose clothing and move out of the heat.
Skip hot showers, alcohol and hard exercise until things settle, since they can make itching and flushing worse.
Try not to scratch, which can break the skin and invite infection.
Take photos of the rash and write down what you ate, applied or took, with times.
p_after: Ask a doctor or pharmacist which allergy medicine is appropriate for you before taking anything new, particularly for children, during pregnancy, with other health conditions or with other medications. Some allergy medicines cause drowsiness, which matters around the pool, the ocean or a rental car.
Do not stop an important prescription on your own, but contact a doctor promptly if you think it caused the reaction.

sections.h2: When to see a doctor in Cabo
p: Arrange a medical visit soon if:
list: Hives cover a large area, keep coming back or last more than a day or two
Itching keeps you from sleeping or enjoying your day
Your eyelids or face are mildly swollen (any tongue or throat swelling means 911)
You have a fever, joint pain, or welts that are painful, bruised or last in one spot for more than a day
There are blisters, peeling skin or sores in the mouth or eyes, particularly after a new medicine (seek urgent care right away)
The area is warm, spreading, oozing or increasingly painful
You have reacted severely in the past, or you have used your epinephrine and need a replacement after being treated at a hospital

sections.h2: Getting a doctor to your hotel, villa or yacht
p: For non-emergency reactions, you do not have to spend your afternoon looking for a clinic. Our house-call doctor in Cabo San Lucas service is available 24/7 in English and Spanish. The doctor reviews your history, examines your skin and breathing, discusses likely triggers and recommends treatment or a referral if needed.
Typical arrival is about 30–45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas and the Tourist Corridor, and up to about 60 minutes in San José del Cabo, Pedregal and Palmilla. All prices are in USD with tax included:

p: A little preparation lowers the chance of a bad surprise:
list: Pack your prescribed epinephrine auto-injectors in your carry-on, ideally two, and keep them out of direct heat. Do not leave them in a hot car or beach bag in the sun.
Bring your usual allergy medicines in labeled packaging, plus a list of your allergies and their generic drug names.
Learn a few phrases: Soy alérgico/alérgica a los mariscos (I am allergic to shellfish) or cacahuates (peanuts).
Tell restaurant staff, tour operators and villa chefs about your allergy before ordering.
Make sure your travel companions know where your auto-injector is and when to call 911.

faq.q: Can I get a doctor for hives at my hotel in Cabo?
faq.a: Yes. A house call costs $189 USD, tax included, and is available 24/7 in English and Spanish. If you have trouble breathing, throat or tongue swelling or feel faint, call 911 instead of waiting for a house call.

faq.q: How do I know if an allergic reaction is an emergency?
faq.a: Call 911 for breathing difficulty, wheezing, swelling of the tongue or throat, trouble swallowing, fainting, confusion, or hives combined with sudden vomiting or weakness. Use a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector right away and still get emergency care.

faq.q: Can a video consultation work for a rash?
faq.a: It can help with a mild rash when you can show it clearly on camera and have no warning signs. A video consultation is $59 USD, tax included. The doctor may recommend an in-person visit if an examination is needed.

faq.q: Why did I break out in hives on vacation?
faq.a: Possible causes include new foods, medicines, stings, sunscreens, heat, sunlight or a viral infection, and sometimes no cause is found. Photos and a timeline of what you ate, applied and took can help a doctor narrow it down.
